model_meta.system_name: Nut-Rotating Ball Screw with Retaining Pieces
model_meta.description: Inferred conceptual model of a nut-rotating ball screw. Opposed helical grooves and metal return tubes define closed circulation routes for load balls; interposed retaining pieces separate adjacent balls.

subsystems.description: Screw shaft with an outer-periphery helical ball rolling groove; in the described embodiment, the shaft is supported horizontally and fixed.
Nut fitted around the screw shaft with an inner-periphery helical groove; configured to rotate relative to the screw shaft.
Ball rolling route formed between mutually opposed helical grooves on the shaft and nut.
Plural metal tubular paths disposed on the nut connect ends of ball rolling paths; their positions are multiple and phase-shifted in the nut peripheral direction.
Load balls roll in the groove-defined portions and circulate within endless paths, applying power-transmission loads while in the rolling path.

Pieces positioned between adjacent load balls; disclosed dependent features include synthetic resin, substantially disk shape, smaller outside diameter, and spherical recesses at axial ends for sliding contact with adjacent balls.

item_flows.name: Load-ball circulation
item_flows.notes: Closed route comprising groove-defined ball rolling path and return tube(s); no separate inter-subsystem connection is implied by this aggregate route.

item_flows.name: Nut rotation relative to shaft
item_flows.notes: Claim 1 specifies a nut-rotation configuration; drive source details are not included in this model.

item_flows.name: Retaining-piece contact with adjacent load balls
item_flows.notes: Claim 5 describes spherical recesses receiving partial ball surfaces and sliding contact.

actions.name: Circulate load balls and transmit load

steps.description: Relative helical motion of nut and screw shaft causes load balls to roll along the groove-defined ball rolling path.
Load balls move through return tubes connecting the rolling-path ends and continue around the endless circulation route.
Load balls in the ball rolling path receive power-transmission loads.
Place retaining pieces between mutually adjacent load balls in the endless circulation path.

In the described embodiment, adjacent ball surface portions fit the retaining-piece recesses and slide against the pieces; the patent describes this arrangement as restricting mutual rubbing and side-by-side arrangement at the scoop-up portion.
